output.summary: KEP-3836 proposes that kube-proxy fail its healthz (and the cloud load balancer health check) for terminating Nodes, signalled by the ToBeDeletedByClusterAutoscaler taint, so load balancers can drain connections; it also adds a /livez path that keeps the old healthz semantics. The KEP is implemented and stable.
output.rationale: For externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster services, kube-proxy's healthz only reports whether data-plane programming is stale, so a terminating Node keeps receiving load-balancer traffic and in-flight connections are cut off. The KEP makes kube-proxy report unhealthy when the Node is being deleted, using the cluster autoscaler taint as the signal because .spec.unschedulable would break ingress for cordoned clusters. A separate /livez endpoint lets vendors keep a liveness probe that is unaffected by node termination.

alternatives.why_not: Users can cordon all nodes at a given moment, which would cause ingress traffic for all eTP:Cluster services to break.

alternatives.option: Align cloud provider health checks for eTP:Cluster services
alternatives.why_not: Non-goal: cloud providers have valid reasons to implement health checks differently; the KEP instead proposes a guidance document.

alternatives.option: Include healthz state in eTP:Local health check answers
alternatives.why_not: Treated as a bug to fix directly rather than through the KEP cycle, per the non-goals section.

evidence.quote: Given that the CA taints the Node which is to be downscaled and deleted, with the taint: `ToBeDeletedByClusterAutoscaler` it would seem most appropriate to use that here.
Using `.spec.unschedulable` as this signal would cause ingress traffic for all `eTP:Cluster` services to break.
adds a `/livez` path to its health check server (`proxier_health.go`) corresponding to the old healthz semantics
if we modify `/healthz` to fail when this taint gets added on the Node, then the `livenessProbe` will fail, causing the Kubelet to restart the Pod until the Node is deleted.
